title: Nehemiah
summary: Nehemiah is a biblical book focused on Jerusalem restoration, wall rebuilding, Torah renewal, and communal reform.
historical_context: Nehemiah narrates Jerusalem's rebuilding and the community's renewed attention to Torah.
ancient_near_east_context: Nehemiah belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Nehemiah should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Nehemiah as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Historical Books, book 11 of 12, Nehemiah contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting Jerusalem restoration, wall rebuilding, Torah renewal, and communal reform to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Nehemiah as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Nehemiah uses narrative within Historical Books, book 11 of 12 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Nehemiah helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Many scholars read the books as later historiographical or Deuteronomistic shaping
date_ranges: Historical span from settlement through exile
Final form often placed in the exilic or post-exilic period
original_audience: Israel and Judah remembering the land, monarchy, and exile
historical_setting: Settlement, monarchy, and exile in the land of Israel and Judah
canonical_role: Nehemiah anchors Jerusalem restoration, wall rebuilding, Torah renewal, and communal reform within Historical Books, book 11 of 12 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How conquest, kingship, and exile are narrated theologically
